matrix.note: Which client, relay and discovery versions work together, as section 17 requires it to be explicit. The first tier is the backward-compatible one: a network tier is deployed before a client that needs its new behaviour, and the compatible tier is kept for the installed-client window below. A version outside every tier is answered with a route error naming the alternatives, which is a bounded loss of one path and never a change to host authority.

tiers.note: The tier every supported client can reach. It is deployed first and retired last. The client range is the package versions a host declares; the relay and discovery ranges are the services as deployed.
